_what: Which Kokoro voice speaks each surface of the practice site.
_why: Owner decisions: (1) ship Kokoro site-wide to eliminate the browser's robotic speechSynthesis, (2) use a MIX of voices so it feels like a team of teachers rather than one voice, (3) AMERICAN ACCENT ONLY — this is an American-English programme, no British voices anywhere, (4) every voice must be CLEARLY intelligible — a student reported that the previous grammar voice was 'annoying' and 'his accent not clear'.
_rule: Every voice id must start with af_ (American female) or am_ (American male). bf_/bm_ (British) are FORBIDDEN and validate_cast() fails the build if any appears.
_how_these_were_chosen: MEASURED, not picked from adjectives. scripts/benchmark_voices.py renders the same 10 sentences (A1 grammar patterns plus longer prose) with all 9 American male and 11 American female Kokoro voices at speed 1.0, transcribes each with an ASR, and reports word-for-word recovery, word error rate and mean ASR confidence. Confidence is the discriminator: every strong voice reaches 100% exact, but they differ in how clearly they get there. The previous cast was assembled from the descriptions in generate_audio.py, which is how the least clear voice in the whole set ended up teaching grammar.

_measured_2026_08_31._note: conf = mean ASR avg_logprob, closer to 0 is clearer. All voices below reached 100% exact recovery unless stated.

_changes_2026_08_31.grammar: am_michael (-0.36, 6th of 9 males) -> am_eric (-0.30, 3rd). This is the voice the student complained about. am_fenrir scored marginally better (-0.29) but speaks at 223 wpm against am_eric's 201, and a grammar explanation for A1 learners should not be the fastest voice in the set. am_adam was not reused here because it already speaks accent and mediation, and the owner asked for a mix of people.
_changes_2026_08_31.review: af_nicole (-0.38, least clear of the whole cast) -> af_kore (-0.30, best female). af_nicole was independently the cause of an earlier defect: at 130 wpm she is a 1.84x outlier, and the pace correction needed to bring her to a C1 target hit the renderer's speed clamp and shipped a clip at 152 wpm.
_changes_2026_08_31.index: af_sky (-0.35) -> af_aoede (-0.31). The host voice is the first thing a student hears each day.
_changes_2026_08_31.listening_rotation: am_michael -> am_eric and af_nicole -> af_kore, for the same reasons. The other three were already in the clearest tier.

_american_voices_available.af_kore: US female, clear and even — best measured female
_american_voices_available.am_adam: US male, professional, neutral — best measured voice overall
_american_voices_available.af_nicole: US female, calm, mature — RETIRED from the cast, least clear measured
_american_voices_available.af_sky: US female, young, friendly — retired from the cast
_american_voices_available.am_michael: US male, warm, conversational — RETIRED from the cast, reported unclear by a student and measured 6th of 9

index.role: Host — opens each day, friendly and welcoming

accent.role: Pronunciation model — the clearest measured voice in the whole set, and the one students imitate

shadowing.role: Main narrator — the passage students shadow

vocab.role: Vocabulary coach — crisp, clear single words

reading.role: Storyteller — narrates reading passages with energy

grammar.role: Grammar teacher — even and articulate, at a moderate pace for A1 learners

mediation.role: Explainer — relays and simplifies (reuses the clear neutral male)

review.role: Reviewer — calm weekly recap, clearest measured female

listening_rotation._note: Listening comprehension needs DIFFERENT PEOPLE, not one voice. Listening items rotate deterministically across this set (by page) so a student practises understanding several American speakers, male and female. Every voice here is in the clearest measured tier.
